correctness.rationale: Seed robustness follows from both extremal social-input bounds. The coordinatewise-monotone outsider map has nondecreasing lower and nonincreasing upper extremal trajectories. Induction and the strict-exposure complement obstruction prove these trajectories settle at the two one-sided bootstrap closures exactly. Sandwiched arbitrary trajectories establish the intersection theorem; endpoint equality is handled without claiming finite crossing. Exact matrix calculation and a two-seed minimum prove the four-agent sharp witness. The standalone rational checker independently confirms the finite witness, not the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The checked November 2026 source gives only a sufficient max-threshold cascade for three or more actions; our theorem is a necessary-and-sufficient characterization by two independent bootstrap closures, with a minimal rational four-agent discrepancy. A dedicated semantic record search and relevant adjacent models found no covering implication. The July 2026 source full text was inaccessible, so historical-priority uncertainty is disclosed.
residual_risks: The full manuscript of arXiv:2607.16036v1 was not accessible for direct passage-by-passage comparison, though its public abstract and model description were checked.
The closely related later preprint was publicly released on 2026-11-16; it is used to compare published implications rather than as the earlier mathematical foundation.
Unindexed papers and stronger nonlinear order-theory treatments could conceivably subsume the special three-bin theorem; no such covering instance was established.
The selected arbitrary three-bin thresholds need not each be realizable as a signaling equilibrium.

value.rationale: A necessary-and-sufficient finite algorithm computes all unavoidable moderate-action adopters, whereas previously established combined-threshold propagation was sufficient only in the three-action case. The minimum four-agent witness shows a genuine false negative for eventual consensus under the conservative condition. This is a motivated structural propagation theorem on an interpretable network object; it goes beyond routine verification of a small numerical example.
